final_message:
Fixed. The bug was in `src/leap.py`: `is_leap_year` only checked `y % 4 == 0`, so century years like 1900 were wrongly treated as leap years. That also made `days_in_month(1900, 2)` return 29.

The function now follows the full Gregorian rule: divisible by 4, except centuries, unless divisible by 400. All 6 tests pass (two were failing before).

You didn't say what was broken, so I assumed it was the failing tests. If you meant something else, tell me. I haven't committed anything.
